title: Getting started with twoPhaseSens
text: twoPhaseSens compares analytic approaches linear-regression exposure coefficient important continuous adjustment covariates observed Phase-2 subsample. Version 0.1.0 focuses setting : outcome continuous; primary exposure numeric; ordinary Phase-1 covariates fully observed; continuous Phase-2 covariates observed together block; Phase-2 membership recorded 0/1 indicator. package implements six approaches: Naive Phase-1 analysis Complete-case analysis (CCA) Fully conditional specification multiple imputation (FCS-MI) Joint-model multiple imputation (JM-MI) Inverse probability weighting (IPW) Augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW) main purpose method-comparison sensitivity analysis. package automatically decide method best given dataset.

title: Getting started with twoPhaseSens
text: package provides fully synthetic example-data generator. generated data derived MIDUS participant-level study data. example contains: outcome1 outcome2: continuous outcomes; exposure: primary exposure; age sex: fully observed Phase-1 covariates; marker1, marker2, marker3: continuous Phase-2 covariates; phase2: binary Phase-2 indicator. Check Phase-2 structure: supported design, Phase-2 covariates observed together phase2 = 1 missing together phase2 = 0.

title: Getting started with twoPhaseSens
text: single outcome fully supported. keep vignette quick build, example uses Naive, CCA, IPW. substantive work, users can request six methods. returned object stores estimates, analysis specification, settings, available diagnostics.
code: fit_one <- twophase_sensitivity(   data = dat,   outcome = "outcome1",   exposure = "exposure",   covariates = c("age", "sex"),   phase2_covariates = c("marker1", "marker2", "marker3"),   phase2 = "phase2",   methods = c("naive", "cca", "ipw"),   seed = 1001 )  fit_one #> twoPhaseSens analysis #>   Outcomes: outcome1 #>   Exposure: exposure #>   Methods: Naive, CCA, IPW #>   Phase-1 N: 300 #>   Phase-2 N: 201 #>  #>   outcome method  estimate         se   conf_low conf_high      p_value status #>  outcome1  Naive 0.4621799 0.05532648 0.35329675 0.5710630 2.591790e-15     ok #>  outcome1    CCA 0.2812535 0.08226308 0.11900865 0.4434982 7.661356e-04     ok #>  outcome1    IPW 0.2642349 0.08438535 0.09884266 0.4296272 1.740409e-03     ok summary(fit_one) #>    outcome exposure method  estimate         se   conf_low conf_high      p_value  df status message N_phase1 N_phase2 phase2_fraction #> 1 outcome1 exposure  Naive 0.4621799 0.05532648 0.35329675 0.5710630 2.591790e-15 296     ok    <NA>      300      201            0.67 #> 2 outcome1 exposure    CCA 0.2812535 0.08226308 0.11900865 0.4434982 7.661356e-04 194     ok    <NA>      300      201            0.67 #> 3 outcome1 exposure    IPW 0.2642349 0.08438535 0.09884266 0.4296272 1.740409e-03 Inf     ok    <NA>      300      201            0.67 #>   analysis_seed weight_min weight_p99 weight_max weight_cv weight_ess #> 1          1001         NA         NA         NA        NA         NA #> 2          1001         NA         NA         NA        NA         NA #> 3          1001   1.086953    2.17709   2.289151 0.1612134   195.9331

title: Getting started with twoPhaseSens
text: Multiple outcomes analyzed separately using exposure, covariates, Phase-2 variables, requested methods. scalar seed expanded sequentially across outcomes. example, two outcomes use seeds 2001 2002. combined comparison table :
code: fit_two <- twophase_sensitivity(   data = dat,   outcome = c("outcome1", "outcome2"),   exposure = "exposure",   covariates = c("age", "sex"),   phase2_covariates = c("marker1", "marker2", "marker3"),   phase2 = "phase2",   methods = c("naive", "cca", "ipw"),   seed = 2001 ) unique(fit_two$results[c("outcome", "analysis_seed")]) #>    outcome analysis_seed #> 1 outcome1          2001 #> 4 outcome2          2002 tbl_sensitivity(   fit_two,   outcome_labels = c(     outcome1 = "Outcome 1",     outcome2 = "Outcome 2"   ) )

title: Getting started with twoPhaseSens
text: initial release intentionally constrained design methodologically numerically validated. Version 0.1.0 assumes: continuous outcomes; linear-regression target model; numeric primary exposure; fully observed Phase-1 covariates; continuous Phase-2 covariates; Phase-2 covariates observed missing together block; FCS-MI using normal linear-regression imputation; package’s validated selection-model, marker-model, IPW, AIPW structures. initial release yet support logistic, count, survival, multilevel outcome models; partially observed Phase-2 blocks; categorical Phase-2 variables requiring different imputation models; arbitrary nuisance models; automatic method selection.

title: twoPhaseSens 0.1.0
text: Initialized package development scaffold. Generalized validated six-method engine use internal canonical variable roles rather MIDUS-specific variable names. Added initial input validation, S3 result object, diagnostics, provisional sensitivity-table formatter. Added initial tests input structure Naive/CCA equivalence. Finalized initial public API analysis settings: users can analyze one multiple outcomes, choose subset methods, set confidence level, control FCS/JM-MI computation, supply either one reproducible seed outcome-specific seeds. Polished tbl_sensitivity() user-controlled decimal places, outcome/method labels, optional standard-error columns, captions, gtsummary/data-frame output modes. Added plot_sensitivity() plot() support forest plots method-specific estimates confidence intervals, including outcome/method filtering, custom labels, configurable reference lines, fixed free facet scales. Upgraded plot_sensitivity() manuscript publication style, including validated six-method palette, open method-specific symbols, horizontal confidence intervals, dotted null line, right-side coefficient/CI p-value annotations. Completed numerical validation manuscript implementation MIDUS outcomes across six methods. Added synthetic example-data generator full Getting Started vignette. Refined publication forest plots single- multiple-outcome analyses, including portable font handling, outcome facet strips, customizable estimate labels, manuscript-size export guidance. Updated README package metadata release-readiness review. Added runnable examples public API focused regression tests FCS-MI, JM-MI, IPW, AIPW. Expanded R CMD check Ubuntu, Windows, macOS current R, plus R-devel R-oldrel-1 Ubuntu. Verified installation end--end execution built source tarball fresh R library process.
